thread:
maria: Heads up — CI microbench on PR #6811 shows a meaningful perf regression in the batcher benchmarks after the kernel selector changes. failing job: `microbench/batcher_throughput`. delta: ~-12% throughput, p99 latency +28ms. link to artifact: https://ci.redwood/infer/6811/artifacts

kai: ack. which part of the change set? last commit touched kernel_selector::score_matrix and the batch_wait_ms heuristic right?

maria: yes, PR updated the cost model scoring and also relaxed batch wait threshold from 4ms -> 8ms under low-concurrency. suspect interaction with kernel autoselect producing a different kernel path for small seq lengths.

oliver: ci-bot says KV cache hitrate dropped ~4% on same runs (see microbench logs). that could push more work to full attention which worsens latency.

maria: here's the failing excerpt from the microbench run:
```
[RUN microbench/batcher_throughput]
baseline: samples=120 mean=1021.3 items/s p99=9.1ms
PR6811: samples=120 mean=897.8 items/s p99=37.3ms
thresholds: throughput -10% allowed, p99 +15ms allowed -> FAILED
```

jen: can we repro locally with the perf harness? might be noisy on my laptop but worth a quick bisect. command we use: `tools/perf/run_microbench --scenario batcher_throughput --runs 120`

maria: yes repros on my workstation with dockerized harness. i'll run a local bisect to narrow to the commit that flipped kernel selection.

ci-bot: artifact uploaded: https://ci.redwood/infer/6811/logs/microbench/batcher_throughput.log (summary attached)

kai: quick glance at artifacts — kernel chosen diff shows PR picks `matmul_mk8` vs baseline `matmul_mk4` for short-seq models. matmul_mk8 has higher launch overhead for small tokens. that aligns with higher p99.

sebastian: interesting — score_matrix change bumped the mk8 score ahead when estimated seq_len < 64 because of new FLOP estimate. but actual typical seq_len in this benchmark is 8-16 tokens which favors mk4. looks like estimator bias.

maria: bisect update: narrowed to commit 5f3a2e9 where cost_estimator changed. reproduces reliably. patch diff snippet:
```diff
- score = flops / (launch + compute);
+ score = flops / (launch*0.9 + compute);
```
seems the heuristic inadvertently favors higher-launch kernels.

jen: ok open revert PR for that single line? or do we want a patched heuristic that includes seq_len weighting?

oliver: prefer a targeted fix: factor in expected sequence length and kv-hit behavior. a quick revert buys time if release is at risk.

maria: rollout blocker? team, we have a release gating on perf thresholds gating next canary. current failing benchmark is part of the gating suite. I recommend revert to unblock and follow up with proper patch.

kai: i can prepare a revert PR and a follow-up with seq_len-aware scoring and a test case in microbench to prevent regressions.

perf-bot: added regression alert to the perf-dashboard: report id perf/2026-03-18-6811. baseline vs PR diff stored.

jen: thanks. maria — can you add a short reproducer to the PR conversation and attach the artifact so CI owners can fast-track revert?

maria: done — added logs, local run command, and kernel selection debug trace. also included kv cache hit stats. will post revert link when ready.

sebastian: small note for follow-up: add an integration microbench that simulates short-seq + high kv-hit rate to catch this class of error.

maria: agreed. once revert merges we'll create an issue for improved scoring + a unit test under perf/regressions.

jen: 👍 opening the revert PR now (will reference this thread).

kai: thanks all — keeping this thread for final merge/revert notes.
